sa.prompt: Differentiate between active flexibility and passive flexibility, detailing the role of opposite muscle strength and external assistance in each.
sa.model: Active flexibility is the range of motion generated solely by individual muscular effort, depending directly on the strength of muscles on the opposite side of the joint (e.g., strong hamstrings holding a leg elevated in a skating spiral). Passive flexibility is the range of motion achieved with external assistance (e.g., arms, a partner, weights, or rubber bands). Passive flexibility allows a wider range of motion than active flexibility, and athletic training aims to increase active range so it approaches the passive range while maintaining bilateral symmetry.
criteria: Define active flexibility (individual effort, dependent on opposite muscle strength).
Define passive flexibility (achieved via external forces like partners, arms, or bands).
State that passive flexibility yields a wider range and active range should approach passive range.

sa.prompt: List four health and physiological benefits of flexibility mentioned in Section 15.6 and state the recommended minimum training frequency.

Under the FITT principle, there is no upper limit on training frequency, but a minimum of three times per week is recommended.

State that there is no upper limit on training frequency.

sa.prompt: Explain the three sequential phases of Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation (PNF) stretching, including durations and physiological rationale for each phase.
sa.model: PNF stretching bypasses protective muscle and tendon reflexes across three phases: (1) Phase 1 (Passive Stretching): Muscle is pulled/pushed slowly and continuously to the movement limit, preventing muscle spindles from initiating the contractile stretch reflex. (2) Phase 2 (Pre-Tension): Trainee contracts the targeted muscle group isometrically against resistance for approximately 7 seconds. (3) Phase 3 (Passive Stretching): Limb is moved into a deeper stretched position (without pain) and held relaxed for approximately 6 seconds. The entire 3-phase sequence is repeated 3 or 4 times.
criteria: Detail Phase 1: slow passive stretch to movement limit to prevent stretch reflex.
Detail Phase 2: pre-tension isometric contraction against resistance for ~7 seconds.
Detail Phase 3: deeper passive stretch held relaxed for ~6 seconds, repeated 3-4 times.

sa.prompt: Compare dynamic stretching and static stretching in terms of execution mechanics, ideal timing within a workout, and why ballistic stretching should be avoided.
sa.model: Dynamic stretching involves moving joints continuously through full ROM in a controlled manner (e.g., swimmer arm circles, runner leaps), taking 5 to 15 minutes as a pre-workout warm-up. Static stretching involves moving slowly into a stretched hold (10 to 30 seconds, 4 to 6 reps), taking 15 to 60 minutes at the end of practice when muscles are warm and tired. Ballistic stretching (bouncing) must be avoided because bouncing triggers micro-damage to muscle fibers, causing post-exercise soreness.
criteria: Describe dynamic stretching (controlled fluid movement, pre-workout warm-up, 5-15 min).
Describe static stretching (slow hold for 10-30s, 4-6 reps, end of practice when warm/tired, 15-60 min).
Explain why ballistic stretching is avoided (bouncing causes muscle fiber micro-damage and soreness).

sa.prompt: Explain the concept of 'joint specificity' in flexibility and describe how it applies to interpreting sit-and-reach test results.
sa.model: Joint specificity means that flexibility is unique to each individual joint or articulation, determined by local bone geometry, joint capsule tautness, and surrounding muscle length. Consequently, an individual may possess high flexibility in one joint (e.g., shoulders) while having tight muscles in another (e.g., hips). When interpreting sit-and-reach test results, a practitioner must recognize that the score evaluates forward flexion of the lower back and hamstrings specifically, rather than serving as an absolute measure of mobility across all body joints.

Identify local determinants (bone structure, capsule, muscle length).

sa.prompt: Describe the testing procedure for the sit-and-reach test, emphasizing the pre-testing preparation rule and what fitness component it measures.

Once warmed up, the participant reaches forward smoothly along a measuring scale without ballistic bouncing, and the maximal distance reached is recorded.
criteria: Identify the sit-and-reach test as measuring forward flexion (lower back and hamstrings).
